title: Entry Coordination in Auctions with Entry Costs
venue: Revision requested by Games and Economic Behavior.
takeaway: Private entry recommendations let the seller capture all surplus net of entry costs by randomizing between the efficient entrant count and one more.

title: When to Hire an Influencer?
takeaway: A paid influencer is profitable only when effort costs are low and the share of inexperienced consumers is positive but not too large.

title: The International Politics of Debris in Earth’s Orbit: A Mechanism Design Approach
takeaway: Without credible enforcement, free-riding reduces debris agreements to the anarchic outcome; conditioning orbital access on participation can support more efficient cooperation.

title: Default Rules and Whistleblowing with Covert Evidence Acquisition
takeaway: Under covert verification, deny-by-default improves receiver welfare only by inducing more testing, while whistleblowing matters only with voluntary certification.

title: Higher Verification Costs Can Support More Disclosure
takeaway: Higher verification costs can increase favorable disclosure because harsher inferences from silence induce the sender to verify more often.

title: Persuade Before Evidence
takeaway: Early public persuasion can crowd out hard-evidence acquisition and leave the receiver less informed, so restricting pre-trial publicity may improve welfare.

title: Rewarding Bad News: Optimal Evidence Rules with Covert Verification
